reasons.D: Uses the passage's inclusive 'we/our' stance, mixes short declaratives with longer periodic sentences, and has the same dry, affectionate irony and period diction ('It matters not'), without laying it on too thick.
reasons.C: Period register and gentle wit are right, and the sentence lengths vary well, but it is more epigrammatic and more polished than the author (a semicolon, a neat closing antithesis) and lacks the author's first-person-plural stance.
reasons.B: Period diction fits, but the sentences are long and even with few of the author's short blunt declaratives, and the tone is smoother and more expository than the passage's quick, amused turns.
reasons.A: Modern register ('I think', plain contemporary diction, 'coarseness', 'loud') with a flat, analytical stance and colon-led lists; it reads as a present-day essayist, not the author.
